beat_loop.pad.description: The six BEAT LOOP buttons, left to right.

images.evidence: In emulation (2026-10-12, stock v1.15, the 2DG blit log): each pad's normal, lit and greyed-out images are drawn into the screen at its position, 80x53, with a colour key (the screen shows through where an image holds the key colour). The pressed, lit and pressed, and lit and greyed-out images were not drawn in these runs (touches held 3 s, with and without a track); their names follow their order in the block, as for the others. The 36 images are one block (0x34F940 to 0x39A1C0) that no code reads at start-up, in update mode, or while installing in either direction (a CPU read watch in the stage-7 rehearsals, docs/xdj700-flashing.md, section 5; the display's 2D engine, which draws them, is not watched); they are drawn when PERFORM is.

beat_loop.pads.title: BEAT LOOP pads (1/2, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16)
beat_loop.pads.does: Six pads; touching one starts a loop of its length (the BEAT LOOP table, decoded 0xD6220: list indices 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 = 1/2 to 16 beats) and it lights; touching it again keeps the loop. The zone is split into sixths (edges, decoded 0xD6250: 83, 166, 250, 333, 416, 500). With SLIP on the pads show SLIP LOOP lengths 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, 1, 1/3, 3/4 (table 0xD6238: indices 3, 4, 6, 8, 5, 7) from another set of images.
beat_loop.pads.evidence: In emulation (2026-10-15, stock v1.15): touching the zone ran its handler (a breakpoint) and the frame changed as described; the record is part of the touch layout, which no code reads at start-up. Its images were drawn at this position (the 2D engine's blit log), and no code reads them at start-up (a CPU read watch).
